proposal.hypothesis: Grouping four complete rows per CTA for widths up to 1024, and two rows with eight warps for wider rows, may reduce CTA scheduling overhead while keeping per-thread work bounded for the wider case. A masked power-of-two column tile and per-row max-subtracted FP32 reductions preserve tail handling and stable softmax; grouping can still hurt occupancy or increase resource use, so the controller must measure it.

retained: Replace the sequence of PyTorch row operations with one fused Triton kernel that performs max-subtracted FP32 softmax per row.
Assign four independent complete rows to each CTA for padded widths through 1024; use two rows and eight warps for wider rows.
Use input and output strides plus row/column masks to support non-contiguous 2D tensors and partial row/column tiles.
